title: Cross-functional canary syllabus and ops scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, cross-functional syllabus (working notes) for running small, observable canaries and A/Bs for latency-sensitive LLM features. Keep it lightweight: the goal is reliable signal early, clear human handoffs, and defined rollback thresholds so teams can iterate without wide blast radius.

Audience:
- Product leads, release stewards, and traffic stewards
- Eng owners (frontend, backend, serving runtime, routing)
- SRE/observability and solutions eng
- Customer-success/solutions for enterprise rollouts

Scope and constraints:
- Focused on feature-level model changes, routing variants, and per-route policy experiments (not infra-only capacity tests).
- Intended for canaries / microreleases (<= 1% global traffic, ramp to 10% max).
- Prefer short windows with live metrics + scheduled steward checks rather than fully automated rollouts for first 3 waves.

Syllabus (phases and cadence):
1) Day -7 to -1: Prep and preflight
   - Define hypothesis and success metrics (primary + 2-3 secondary).
   - Register experiment in rollout ledger (JIRA ticket + artifact links).
   - Create telemetry workbook with dashboards and baseline snapshots (24/7 baseline for last 14 days).
   - Identify slices (geo, client tier, route, input length buckets).
   - Run local integration smoke and synthetic traffic that targets edge slices.

2) Day 0: Launch wave 0 (synthetic + internal)
   - Traffic: synthetic + 0.1% internal beta users.
   - Observation window: 30–60m.
   - Gate: no increase in request error-rate above 1% relative to baseline; latency p95 regression < 20%.
   - Human check-in: steward posts observations in #rollouts with quick snapshot.

3) Day 1–3: Wave 1 (pilot customers / early adopters)
   - Traffic: 0.5–1% of production, targeted cohort.
   - Observation windows: rolling 2h, formal steward check every 4h.
   - Gate rules: see gating section.
   - If green, schedule progressive ramp; if amber, hold and debug; if red, initiate rollback.

4) Day 4–7: Ramp windows
   - Incremental ramps (1% -> 3% -> 5% -> 10%), each with 4–8h observation and a steward sign-off.
   - After 10%, switch to automated guardrails for 24–72h observation, then decision for wider launch.

Pre-launch checklist (short):
- [ ] Hypothesis + owner + duration documented
- [ ] Baseline dashboards created and shared
- [ ] Slice definitions and tagging rules agreed
- [ ] Rollback procedure and playbook linked in ticket
- [ ] On-call/incident contacts tagged and paged test passed
- [ ] Synthetic traffic test results attached

Slice design pattern examples (prefer explicit naming):
- CLIENT_TIER: free | pro | enterprise
- INPUT_LEN: short (<64), medium (64–512), long (>512)
- REGION: NA | EU | APAC
- ROUTE_TYPE: search | chat | rerank

Metric grouping and recommended primary signals:
- Safety/quality: semantic-failure-rate, moderation-trigger-rate, human review flag rate
- Correctness: exact-match/precision proxies, rerank click delta (if available)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 request time, tail queue depth, KV cache hit-rate
- Reliability: request error-rate (4xx/5xx), retry volume, connection drops
- Cost: tokens-per-request, GPU-seconds-per-request (for Dedicated customers)
- User impact: conversion delta, retention proxy, NPS attribution (if available)

Gating thresholds (examples, conservative by default):
- Immediate red (auto-rollback): absolute increase in request error-rate >= 2 percentage points, or p95 latency regression > 50% (compared to baseline window).
- High-severity amber (pause + investigate): relative deterioration in semantic-failure-rate > 30% with clear user-visible regressions on core routes.
- Green: changes within +/- 5% of baseline on primary metrics and no safety flags.

Observation windows and statistical notes:
- Use rolling windows matched to traffic volume. For low-volume slices, extend windows to 24–48h before definitive decisions.
- Avoid overinterpreting noisy short-term deltas on small slices — require consistent direction across adjacent windows.
- Predefine minimum sample sizes for signal validity (e.g., >500 requests per slice per window).

Human roles and responsibilities (short roster):
- Release Steward: owner of the experiment, convenes sign-offs and posts cadence notes.
- Traffic Steward: runs ramps, executes traffic split changes, records timestamps.
- Eng Owner (serving/runtime): triages infra/latency issues and coordinates hotfixes.
- Observability Lead: ensures dashboards are live, stitches traces on request.
- Customer Success Liaison: monitors enterprise customers in the cohort and surfaces qualitative feedback.

Communication templates (use when posting to #rollouts or stakeholders):
Slack subject: [CANARY] <short-feature> wave <n> — <owner initials>
Slack body template:
- Feature: <short description>
- Traffic: <percent> -> <target cohort>
- Current primary signals: error-rate <x>, p95 <y>ms, semantic-failure <z>%
- Status: GREEN / AMBER / RED
- Action: <next step — ramp/hold/rollback>
- Link: <dashboards / ticket / runbook>

Rollback playbook (short):
1) Traffic steward executes traffic revert to last stable variant (document exact timestamp).
2) Steward posts rollback notice in #rollouts with immediate paging of oncall if error-rate spike triggered rollback.
3) Oncall/eng owner triages logs/traces; if related to model outputs, attach sample payloads (redaction allowed) to ticket.
4) Postmortem window: initial 48-hour notes, full retro within 7 days.

Lightweight experimental analysis checklist (post ramp):
- Compare pre/post distributions for primary signals and top-3 slices by volume.
- Run A/A sanity on a subset where feasible to validate instrumentation.
- Gather qualitative notes from CS for enterprise cohort.
- If effect uncertain, schedule a 1-week extended-canary with targeted telemetry.

Common failure modes and mitigations (field notes):
- Oscillation during ramp: add a cooling period (min 30m) and reduce ramp step size.
- False positives from outlier client: quarantine the client slice and retest.
- Telemetry lag: avoid decisions until backend pipeline catch-up completes; mark windows as provisional.

Open questions to resolve before standardizing this syllabus:
- How to encode minimum sample size checks into Console guardrails? (observability team)
- Where to centralize A/B experiment metadata so non-owners can discover active experiments? (product + infra)
- Mechanism for automating rollback triggered by composite safety signals vs single-metric rules? (SRE + ai-safety)

Immediate action items (owner: Maya):
- [ ] Publish this draft and solicit feedback from SRE and Observability this week
- [ ] Prototype a compact dashboard template for 3 primary signals
- [ ] Attach example slack and incident templates to JIRA-RW-3412

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Keep playbooks short; link to full runbooks for operator steps.
- Experiment naming: feature_shortname.date.waveN — makes logs easier to grep.
- For private deployments, coordinate with customer infra lead ±48h for ramp windows.

Appendix: quick examples
- Example guardrail snippet: if semantic-failure-rate_delta > 0.25 and samples > 1000 -> AMBER.
- Example naming: longcontext-respell-2025-02-wave1

End of scratchpad.
